program.how: written for ounce-core from the algorithm in the paper; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: SipHash-2-4 with key 00 01 .. 0f and the 15-byte message 00 01 .. 0e outputs a129ca6149be45e5 (the paper's worked example)
SipHash-2-4 with the same key and the messages of length 0 to 63 (bytes 00 01 02 ...) outputs the 64 published reference values

expected_values_source.what: the 64 SipHash-2-4 (64-bit) known-answer outputs in vectors.h of the authors' reference repository; the 15-byte value is from the paper
expected_values_source.note: the vectors are data, copied as numbers; the file's code was not copied

negative_control: built with SIP_C=1 (one compression round instead of two), 0 of 64 vectors match and the program exits 1
not_checked: the paper's security claims (PRF strength, resistance to hash flooding)
speed figures (emulator run time says nothing about the authors' hardware)
SipHash variants other than 2-4 and the 128-bit output version
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces exactly the published SipHash-2-4 outputs for 65 inputs. It does not show the security claims hold.
